data.name: Adnaanun
data.gender_notes: Adnaanun is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'adnā', meaning 'to serve', 'to help' or 'to offer'. Adnaanun is a name of Arabic origin, used in the Islamic religion. It is a powerful name, signifying someone who is a giver, a helper, or one who offers assistance. The name Adnaanun carries the meaning “Giver or Helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Adnaanun usually hope their child will grow to embody giver or helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Adnaanun is a name of spiritual significance in Islam. It symbolizes selflessness, generosity, and the desire to serve others. It is a reminder of the importance of helping and supporting those around us, and of the spiritual reward that comes from doing so.
data.etymology: Adnaanun belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Giver or Helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adnaanun total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: أَدْنَانٌ
in_arabic.long_meaning: أَدْنَانٌ هو اسم عربي يُقصد به الشخص الذي يتمتع بالنعمة والقرب من الله تعالى، ويكون له علاقة وثيقية بالفرد المبارك، حيث يُعتبر أَدْنَانٌ من أسماء الله الحسنى التي تُستخدم في الحالات الخاصة. يُشير أَدْنَانٌ إلى الفرد الذي تمتع بالنعمة من الله، ويكون قريبًا من الله تعالى، ويعبأ بأعماله الصالحة، ويكون محبًا لله تعالى. يُعتبر أَدْنَانٌ من الأسماء التي تُستخدم في الحالات الخاصة، مثل: عند ولادة مولود، أو عند إنجاب مولود، أو عند ذكر الله تعالى في الصلاة، أو عند إحياء مناسبات خاصة.

in_english.long_meaning: Adnaanun is an Arabic name that signifies nearness to God and divine favor. It is a name that conveys a sense of closeness to Allah and His blessings. In Islamic tradition, Adnaanun is a name that symbolizes the individual's closeness to God and their ability to receive divine favor. Those named Adnaanun are believed to possess a unique connection to Allah and are often associated with spiritual growth and development. The name Adnaanun has its roots in Arabic and is derived from the word 'dunya', which means 'worldly life'.

By bearing thisname, one is constantly reminded of their spiritual duty to help, serve, and assist others, in turn coming closer to God.

historical_references.reference:
Adnan was the ancestor of the Arab tribes of the Quraysh, according to Islamic tradition. He is believed to have lived around the 4th century AD and is considered to be the great-grandfather of Prophet Muhammad.
Context: Ancestry of the Prophet Muhammad and the Arab tribes of Mecca.

Adnan ibn Tuwayb, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, was one of the ten people granted the title of Sahabi (companion) based on his close friendship and companionship with the Prophet during the early days of Islam. He is believed to have lived around the 7th century AD.
Context: Early companions of Prophet Muhammad in Medina.
